 Photo credit: © Matt Marton-Imagn Images By  Jeff Paterson Nov 16, 2026, 13:00 EST Updated: Nov 16, 2026, 12:17 EST Comments Add to Preferred Sources The Vancouver Canuck s (4-17-1) shoot for consecutive wins for the first time all season when they visit the Utah Mammoth (10-8-3) at Delta Center. Tonight’s game starts at 7:30 pm PCT. The Canucks snapped a seven-game losing streak with a 6-3 win in Las Vegas on Sunday night. It was just the second win for the club in its last 19 outings. What we know 
 With back-to-back games, the Canucks did not hold a morning skate in Salt Lake City. Nikita Tolopilo, recalled from AHL Abbotsford on Saturday, is expected to make his NHL season debut in goal . Tolopilo is 7-2-2 in the minors this season with a 2.52 GAA and an .897 save percentage. It’s unclear at this point who will serve as the backup. Last night, Leevi Meriläinen stopped 34 of 37 shots to help the Canucks beat Vegas. Filip Chytil scored his first two goals of the season and his first NHL goals since October 16, 2025, at Dallas. Linus Karlsson also scored twice and established a career-high with seven shots on goal. For the second straight game, Elias Pettersson opened the scoring, and Drew O’Connor scored just his second goal in the past 19 games when he converted in the third period. In all, 12 different Canucks skaters found the scoresheet as the team went wire to wire to win for the first time this season (opening the scoring and was never tied after that).  Brock Boeser had a pair of first period assists on goals by Pettersson and Chytil and now has eight points on a seven-game point streak. He is two games shy of matching his career-high for consecutive games with a point. This is the third set of back-to-back games for the Canucks this season. They are 0-2 in the second half of the previous two with losses at home to Vegas and in New York against the Rangers. After a game in Seattle on Thursday to close out this road trip, the Canucks will host Minnesota and Chicago for back-to-back games next weekend. For the second time this month, a pair of Canucks are celebrating birthdays on the same day. On November 2, it was Luke Schenn and Filip Hronek. This time, it’s Paul Cotter and Linus Karlsson who both turn 27 today. The Opponent 
 The Mammoth are struggling to deal with a rash of injuries to their top players. Nick Schmaltz, Dylan Guenther and Logan Cooley are all out of the lineup, taking three of the team’s top five scorers out of action. The club is also missing former Canuck Nate Schmidt along with John Marino on defence. Brogan Houston @ houston_brogan · Follow Utah Mammoth injury updates, per André Tourigny:
• Logan Cooley: Day to day. "Nothing long-term," but he isn't playing today. "Hopefully we can have him pretty soon."
• Dylan Guenther: No changes. "On schedule."
• Nick Schmaltz: No timeline yet. "Should have news soon."
•   Show more 
 6:40 PM · Nov 14, 2026 97 Reply Copy link Read 3 replies Utah has lost five straight, although three of those games have extended beyond regulation time. The Mammoth fell 6-5 in a five-round shootout at home to San Jose on Saturday. Zac Jones scored twice, and Mikhail Sergachev had a goal and an assist. It’s the first time since the franchise relocated to Salt Lake City that the Mammoth got three goals in the same game from defencemen. Jack McBain and Barrett Hayton scored the other goals against the Sharks. Clayton Keller had two assists against the Sharks and leads Utah in scoring with 27 points. The injured trio of Cooley (11), Schmaltz (9) and Guenther (6) have combined for 26 goals. Without those three in the lineup, Utah’s leading goal scorer is Sergachev with six goals on the season. Utah has the second-best power play in the league, running at 34.7%. However, Cooley, Schmaltz and Guenther account for 16 of the team’s 25 goals with the man advantage this season. They did manage to score a pair of power play goals against San Jose. Karel Vejmelka allowed five goals on 21 shots on Saturday. Expect Sebastian Cossa to get the start in goal tonight. The Mammoth started the season 7-3, but with the injury issues, the team has just three wins in its last 11 games (3-5-3). Tonight will be the first time the Canucks face former head coach Adam Foote since he was dismissed following last season. Foote landed as an assistant coach on Andre Tourigny’s staff.  News and notes 
 Utah swept the three-game season series with the Canucks last season and has won all six head-to-head matchups since relocating from Arizona ahead of the 2025-26 season.
